title: Random forests classify CT-derived COVID severity in a retrospective cohort
summary: A random forest used patient-level aggregates of CT texture features to distinguish four COVID severity groups in 956 patients from the MosMed dataset. Reported overall accuracy was 90.95%. Eight-fold validation was selected after comparing fold configurations, which can make performance optimistic. This retrospective severity-classification study does not establish prospective triage safety or clinical benefit.
organization: Shahid Beheshti University of Medical Sciences

source_review.scope: Primary relevant Methods/results/limitations and exact front/canonical identity; current primary PubMed linked correction/retraction metadata checked.

evidence.tested: Patient-level CT feature aggregation, internal cross-validation and severity-reference comparisons.
evidence.unknown: External validation and prospective clinical utility remain unestablished; selection among validation configurations can bias performance.
evidence.ai_role: A 40-tree random forest learns severity relationships from aggregated CT texture measurements, compared with LDA and nearest-neighbor classifiers.
